newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian debt futures remain under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt futures remain under pressure.

text.p: *Australian bond futures were under pressure across the curve as speculative trades were unwound after the Reserve Bank left policy unchanged after Tuesday's board meeting.
*April labour force, RBA's Macfarlane testimony on Thursday.
Australian debt futures were under pressure across the curve as speculative trades were unwound after the Reserve Bank left policy unchanged after Tuesday's board meeting.

June bill futures dropped back into line with current official 6.0 percent official interest rates, while further forward contracts started to price in the possibility of a tightening in the fourth quarter 1997 and first quarter 1998.
Traders said the reaction to the RBA's on-hold stance was largely in the futures market, and cash bill rates in particular showed little movement.
"Although the chances of a cut were small, the futures market had been priced reasonably cheap to take advantage of risk/reward trades," said one short-end trader.
The risk was for a small fall on an unchanged policy, and a greater reward if the central bank had eased, he added.

The focus now switches to RBA governor Macfarlane's first semi-annual testimony to a parliamentry finance committee, and his comments will be heavily scrutinised for the central bank's current thinking on policy and the economy in general.
The April labour force report will also be released on Thursday and is expected to show a strong rebound in employment.

Median forecasts centre on a 35,000 jump in employment, although this is not expected to have an impact on the unemployment rate, which is seen sticking at 8.7 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economist.
A softer bias in U.S. Treasuries both in New York and Tokyo also added to the local heavy tone after a weak response to Tuesday's three-year U.S. note auction.
The U.S. Treasury will offer A$12.0 billion of 10-year notes later on Thursday, the second and final leg of the quarterly refunding auctions.

The market reversed its initial spread tightening against the dollar bloc after the RBA left policy unchanged. Canadian debt had outperformed the U.S. again on Tuesday, while N.Z. bonds were also under pressure from a fall in the N.Z. TWI.
The local yield curve resumed a flattening trend.
